entry.title: Research Summary: September 25, 2026
entry.summary: Agent infrastructure dominates this week. Hermes Bot Screen is the headline: every agent now gets its own full cloud desktop (screen, mouse, keyboard, terminal, browser) on a headless Linux gateway — a major unlock for computer-use and GUI-driving agents. Complementing it, Google's open-source AX brings Kubernetes-style declarative orchestration to autonomous agent workloads at cluster scale. Frontier-model news is verified fresh: GPT-6 Sol and GPT-6 Luna shipped 22 Sep 2026 as descendants of GPT-6 Astra, splitting the flagship between deep reasoning/coding (Sol) and faster general-purpose use (Luna). On the research side, the Just-in-Time Memory paper argues for retrieval-time, task-adaptive memory curation over write-time distillation — directly relevant to long-running Hermes agent design. Practitioner picks round it out: a Jev decision-engine automation pattern (trigger → decide → confidence gate → act) with concrete latency and gating details, Claude Code v2.1.275's new send-now shortcut (Ctrl+Enter or Ctrl+X, Ctrl+S) for interrupting a running agent turn and flushing queued messages, and a guide to four free Jev API routes with the gotchas that matter (model-name confusion, expiring gateway windows, third-party risk).

entry.title: Research Summary: September 24, 2026
entry.summary: This week's research/documentation is dominated by the Hermes-Claude subscription plugin: an end-to-end architectural walkthrough of the pipeline (Hermes → plugin → unmodified official Claude Code execution, with process isolation and an admission relay for billing integrity), paired with a security-focused auth guide confirming credentials stay entirely with the official CLI via claude auth — no API keys for users to store or leak. On the release side, Hermes Agent v0.21.4 adds a --format stream-json flag producing structured JSONL output, immediately useful for automation and tooling, alongside a merged-PR rollup bringing skills auto-load and MCP discovery concurrency improvements. In the broader agent ecosystem, Microsoft Agent Framework 1.19.0 hardens MCP security by scoping sessions per invocation — relevant context for anyone wiring external tools into agent workflows — and the early-stage AgentProto runtime (v0.20.0, Apache-2.0) offers a single interface across 14 coding agents with Hermes listed as a supported integration, an early signal of growing ecosystem interoperability.
